analysis.title: GS Global Equities Call 27 Oct 2026
key_insights: US equities are better bid pre-market (SPX +25bps, NDX +45bps, RTY +30bps) on light news flow. The main headline is a report that Iran's Supreme Leader called for meeting conditions to end the war.
Crude is lower on the Iran headlines (WTI -80bps at $101). Rates are lower as well: UST 2yr -2.5bps at 4.69%, 10yr -1.5bps at 4.975%, 30yr -1bp at 5.29%.
Focus is on earnings and the FOMC meeting. MSFT, GOOG, NOW and KLAC report 10/28. AMZN and INTC report Thursday. FOMC is 10/28.

The AI trade is firmer after yesterday's rally. Tokyo Electron +3%, Hynix +5% and Samsung +4% in Asia. SMH +1% and DRAM +2.5% pre-market. AVGO is +2.4% pre-market after reportedly arranging a $63bn deal to finance chip purchases (Bloomberg).
International movers after results: Novartis +1.5%, HSBC -6%, Reckitt -4%, Mercedes -3%.
Privo on Risk: front-end rates have stabilized, which is good for risk. Energy is too high for comfort but more likely to cause chop than a sustained selloff absent another escalation.
Privo on Risk: credit is the main worry, still flashing yellow to red relative to equities. A calmer credit market could be a meaningful catalyst for a broader rally.

Hyperscaler earnings and the Fed are the main events this week. Four items to watch: capex (flat or up is fine, down would be disastrous for picks-and-shovels names), backlog conversion into revenue, free cash flow in the out quarters, and financing (equity versus debt).

GS's strongest global view is that central banks will deliver fewer hikes than currently priced. Rates strategists cite underweight positioning, diminished technical risks and risk asset pressures as reasons the recent rally might extend.
GS equity strategists are wary of momentum factor exposure given narrow breadth, but expect the S&P 500 to resume its climb after the midterm election as earnings grow solidly.
GS credit strategists are cautious on IG technology bonds but see scope for a near-term reversal in HY after the scale of the recent selloff.
GS FX strategists expect the yen to hedge further AI jitters, partly because such jitters would shrink US-Japan rate differentials.
GS commodity strategists recommend targeted exposure to oil products and European natural gas to hedge near-term escalation, plus longer-term exposure to copper, gold and select power markets.

Global and G3 growth are in line with potential GDP. Fiscal easing and the AI boom have offset the drag from the Iran war and higher US tariffs. 2027 forecasts show more of the same, but risks are skewed to the downside.
Energy prices have climbed again on fears of renewed Middle East escalation. Gasoline, diesel, jet fuel and European/Asian natural gas are near or above their March/April highs.
Longer-term yields have risen by an average of about 100bp across DM curves since early 2026, tied to large deficits, AI-linked borrowing and central bank hikes. The moves have been mostly orderly.

The AI growth impulse was expected to peak in late 2026 or early 2027. AI investment as a share of GDP is expected to slow over the next year, weighing on US capex growth. The AI wealth effect added an estimated 0.4pp (0.25% of GDP) to US consumer spending growth over the past year.
Prime book: Asia-focused fundamental L/S managers are down 8.9% MTD in October (vs MXAP -6.4%) and up 14.5% YTD. Drawdown was led by beta, asset selection, Momentum and Volatility factors.

Global Prime saw large net selling MTD, with short sales well above long sales. Asian equities short sales exceeded long sales 1.7 to 1. Taiwan, Korea and Japan led the selling as hedge funds unwound AI exposure. Info Tech led sector selling, followed by Financials, Comm Services and Industrials. Health Care was the most net bought sector, followed by Materials and Energy.

Asia Fundamental L/S net leverage fell 16.9 points to 48.0% (21st percentile 1-year). Gross leverage was 189.3% (8th percentile 1-year). Korea dominates net selling and de-grossing, with net allocation at 3.4% versus a June peak of about 8%.
Chart of the day: GS Vol Panic Index rose from 4.63 on Wednesday to 7.94 on Friday, reaching the 'panic' threshold for the first time since late July, while the S&P has barely moved.

A capex cut by hyperscalers would be damaging for picks-and-shovels AI names.
Concerns about the sustainability of the AI investment boom have intensified in recent weeks.
Higher long-term yields, about 100bp higher on average across DM curves since early 2026, weigh on global growth.
Narrow market breadth raises momentum factor risk.
Hedge fund de-grossing in Asian AI names, especially Korea and Taiwan.

GS equity strategists are wary of momentum factor exposure given narrow market breadth.

tension_points.bull_case: Capex flat or up is fine, and strong underlying businesses may let hyperscalers fund the next leg with equity over debt. Asian AI names bounced after yesterday's rally.
tension_points.bear_case: Capex down would be disastrous for picks-and-shovels names. Concerns about AI investment sustainability have intensified, and the AI growth impulse is expected to peak in late 2026 or early 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A cut in hyperscaler capex in this week's earnings.

tension_points.bull_case: If credit calms down, it could be a meaningful catalyst for a broader rally, and HY has scope for a near-term reversal after the recent selloff.
tension_points.bear_case: Credit is still flashing yellow to red relative to equities, and GS remains cautious on IG technology bonds.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Credit continuing to deteriorate relative to equities.
